proof_summary: The defining sum satisfies \(a(n+1)=(2^n-1)a(n)+2^{\binom{n+1}{2}}\); for odd prime \(p\), Fermat’s theorem and the identity for \(\binom{n+2(p-1)+1}{2}\) make both the coefficient and forcing term periodic modulo \(p\), so induction applies once the shifted initial value is shown to be \(1\) by vanishing product factors at indices \(p-1\) or \(2(p-1)\). For \(p=2\), the same recurrence directly gives \(a(n)\equiv1\pmod2\) for every \(n\ge1\).
